item.title: How Trump Is Dismantling America’s Scientific Research Machine
item.author: Christopher Flavelle, Irena Hwang, Adam Sella, Alan Blinder, Sheryl Gay Stolberg, Benjamin Mueller and Michael C. Bender
item.content:encoded: The system that has driven life-altering discoveries and helped make the United States a superpower is now under intense strain.

item.title: Carney Says No Hurry on Trade Deal If US Won’t Offer Good Terms
item.author: Stephanie Hughes
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Mark Carney said he won’t rush a trade agreement with the US if the terms aren’t in Canada’s best interests, and suggested he expects his country will still be in President Donald Trump’s crosshairs after the US midterm elections.

item.title: Trump’s Arch Faces New Legal Challenge From Virginia and D.C.
item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: The two jurisdictions contend that President Trump’s proposed 250-foot arch is “flagrantly unlawful,” citing concerns over traffic, the environment and historic preservation.

item.title: Refugees From Ukraine’s Besieged Oleshky Are Returned to Safety
item.author: Kollen Post
item.content:encoded: Refugees from the besieged southern town of Oleshky have returned to free Ukrainian territory and reunited with family members.

item.title: Trump’s Board of Peace Petitions Italy for Gaza Police Support
item.author: Donato Paolo Mancini
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace formally asked Italy to provide advisers from the police, firefighters and the carabinieri corps to help build a new security force for the Gaza Strip, according to letters seen by Bloomberg News.

item.title: Susan Collins Is Always Keeping Score
item.author: Michael Kruse and Lisa Lerer
item.content:encoded: The long-serving senator has delivered millions of dollars to every corner of her state. But in Maine, people say, it’s best to avoid getting on her bad side.

item.title: US Embassy Warns of Mass Casualty Threat at Moscow Museum
item.author: Ros Krasny
item.content:encoded: The US embassy in Moscow said it was “aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event” on Saturday at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow, and was coordinating with Russian authorities on a response.

item.title: Israel’s Election Leaves Netanyahu in Limbo
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Israel Bureau Chief Ethan Bronner tells Bloomberg This Weekend that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor the opposition has a clear path to forming a government after Israel’s election, potentially setting up difficult coalition negotiations or another vote. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Bronner discusses Netanyahu’s political durability, increased Arab voter participation and how another conflict with Iran could alter the coalition calculus. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Kalshi, Polymarket Odds Don't Mimic Midterm Elections 2026 Polls
item.author: Carolyn Silverman, Ella Feldman and Leonardo Nicoletti
item.content:encoded: What may seem like contradictory numbers are, in fact, just two ways to capture a similar picture.

item.title: Bolsonaro Leaves Brazil After Rejecting Election
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Brazil Country Chief Filipe Pacheco tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after refusing to recognize Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory, as Bolsonaro faces multiple investigations in Brazil. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Pacheco explains Bolsonaro’s circuitous journey to Miami, his pledge to lead the opposition from the US and how investors are assessing Lula’s surprise comeback. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Midterm Fight Comes Down to the Final Days
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Balance of Power co-host Joe Mathieu joins Bloomberg This Weekend to break down the final days of campaigning before the midterms, including President Donald Trump’s late push and the House and Senate races that could determine control of Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Meeks Puts Affordability Atop Democrats’ Agenda
item.content:encoded: House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks tells Bloomberg This Weekend that affordability would be Democrats’ top priority if they take control of the House, alongside restoring health-care benefits and conducting oversight of the Trump administration. Speaking with host David Gura, Meeks says companies involved in importing Russian diesel could face congressional scrutiny and predicts Hakeem Jeffries would become speaker if Democrats win the majority. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The AI Backlash Uniting Voters
item.content:encoded: Artificial intelligence is becoming a political issue for the first time in this year’s midterms, with much of the voter backlash focused not on the technology itself but on the data centers needed to power it. Communities from Michigan to Texas are raising concerns about electricity costs, water use and the broader impact of AI on jobs and local economies. Former House Speaker Paul Ryan says data centers have become a proxy for wider fears about AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Publicidad política en español cae antes de elecciones de EE.UU.
item.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
item.content:encoded: Las elecciones de medio término van camino a ser las más caras de la historia, pero los anuncios políticos en español se desploman pese al creciente peso del voto latino.

item.title: Midterm Elections 2026: Spending surge is leaving out Spanish-language ads
item.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
item.content:encoded: The US midterm elections are on track to be the most expensive ever, with ad spending set to top $11 billion, but the share being directed toward Spanish-language advertisements is shrinking dramatically, even with Latino voters seen by both parties as a critical swing group.

item.title: Talarico Makes Final Election Pitch to Texans: ‘You Are My Slingshot’
item.author: Robert Draper
item.content:encoded: The Democratic candidate for Senate has led in polls. But because it’s Texas, he remains the underdog.

item.title: Investors Brace for Post-Midterm Policy Shifts
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Government Analyst Nathan Dean tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the midterm results could reshape congressional oversight while the Trump administration continues pursuing deregulation across banking, crypto and other industries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Dean explains what investors should watch in energy, AI, banking and trade, including the potential for further tariffs and changes that could encourage regional bank consolidation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Affordability Crisis Shaping US Elections
item.content:encoded: The US economy remains resilient, but many Americans are still struggling with the cost of housing, health care, groceries and other necessities. Former House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Kevin Brady and Willett Advisors Chairman & CEO Steven Rattner explain why the gap between strong economic data and household finances has made affordability one of the defining issues of the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Starts at ‘Basically Zero’ in Building Cheap Military Drones
item.author: Andrew Martin and Jen Judson
item.content:encoded: At a manufacturing plant near Salt Lake City with a big American flag on the wall and work stations crammed with tools and parts, dronemaker Vector Defense Inc. is in expansion mode.

item.title: Cost of Living Looms Over the Midterms
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Economics Economic Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy tells Bloomberg This Weekend that higher costs for gasoline, groceries and housing are weighing on voters and putting pressure on parts of the coalition Donald Trump assembled in 2024. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kennedy explains how affordability concerns are playing out in states including Michigan, Iowa and Texas and how control of Congress could shape economic policy after the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Strikes Bashneft Refineries as Russia Attacks Power Grid
item.author: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Ukraine’s drone forces struck a complex of refineries deep within Russia, even as Kyiv and other parts of the country struggled to restore electricity following overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.

item.title: Iran Threatens Wider US Strikes Even as Talks Make Progress
item.author: Patrick Sykes and Eric Martin
item.content:encoded: Iran’s Supreme Leader ordered his top military commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation with the US and Israel and expand Tehran’s options for retaliation, even as his top diplomat signaled progress in diplomatic talks.

item.title: US Midterms: Trumpism May Already Be in Decline Worldwide
item.author: Alan Crawford
item.content:encoded: US elections from Alaska to Maine will reverberate globally next week, as midterm voting promises to diminish a president who has strong-armed the world.

item.title: Pete Ricketts Leads Dan Osborn in Nebraska Senate Race, Poll Finds
item.author: Ruth Igielnik and Emily Davies
item.content:encoded: Voters see Dan Osborn, the independent seeking to unseat Senator Pete Ricketts, as more like a Democrat than an independent, a Times/Siena poll found.

item.title: Trump and GOP Close Midterms With Ugly Personal Attacks
item.author: Tim Balk and Sam Easter
item.content:encoded: Facing backlash over inflation and anger with the president, Republicans have turned to an onslaught of baseless claims about Democratic candidates.

item.title: In Nebraska Senate Race, the Independent May Have an Identity Problem
item.author: Nate Cohn
item.content:encoded: Dan Osborn trails by six points, and voters don’t seem to buy that he’s truly independent from Democrats.

item.title: As Midterms Near, Top Law Firms That Capitulated to Trump Are on the Sidelines
item.author: Michael S. Schmidt and Jim Rutenberg
item.content:encoded: None of the firms that struck deals to avoid crippling executive orders are publicly involved in the major legal efforts to check the Trump administration’s attempts to meddle in the midterm elections, a review by The New York Times shows.

item.title: A Halloween Tale: Ghost Stories of the U.S. Capitol
item.author: Olivia Diaz and Alex Kent
item.content:encoded: The ghost stories, dating back to the 19th century, are fitting for a building where the past rarely stays dead.

item.title: Voters Usually Ignore Corruption as an Issue. It Now Has Their Attention.
item.author: David Ovalle and Emily Cochrane
item.content:encoded: Voters have shrugged off accusations of corruption for years, believing all politicians are corrupt, but thanks to President Trump’s unpopularity and growing wealth, the issue is breaking through.

item.title: Justice Dept. Confirms Alaska Inquiry Even as Its Focus Remains Unclear
item.author: Anna Griffin and Glenn Thrush
item.content:encoded: Democrats and former officials have accused the department of pursuing a political goal in the guise of a legal one: to publicize a scheme, sordid but not illegal under state law, damaging to Democrats.

item.title: Judge Blocks Expediting Migrant Children’s Asylum Cases, For Now
item.author: Madeleine Ngo
item.content:encoded: Lawyers for the children praised the pause on fast-tracked interviews of unaccompanied minors, calling it a blow against the Trump administration’s “deportation assembly line.”

item.title: Alina Habba’s Husband Ignited Drama in Trump’s Circle. Now He’s Under Scrutiny.
item.author: Anatoly Kurmanaev, Tyler Pager and Declan Walsh
item.content:encoded: Turhan Mildon, who married Alina Habba this summer, presents himself as a 29-year-old billionaire with ties to global leaders. His story has inconsistencies.

item.title: Obamacare Policies Hit Again With Steep Premium Increases for 2027
item.author: Reed Abelson and Margot Sanger-Katz
item.content:encoded: Premiums will increase an average 13 percent next year for millions of Americans, on top of an earlier steep increase. It adds to the problems facing the program, which the Trump administration has weakened.

item.title: Trump’s Plane Flyover Is a Halloween Trick for Startled D.C. Residents
item.author: Michael Crowley
item.content:encoded: A White House social media account said the surprise Air Force One flight was part of a Halloween event hosted by the president and the first lady.

item.title: Why Running for the U.S. Senate Is a Rich Person’s Game
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: Your Senate candidates are probably richer than you.

item.title: Polish President Holds Crisis Talks as Court Standoff Grows
item.author: Maciej Martewicz
item.content:encoded: Polish President Karol Nawrocki scheduled emergency consultations with parliamentary parties on Saturday to “restore constitutional order” as an escalating standoff at the country’s top court threatened to spark a political crisis.

item.title: Appeals Court Again Rejects Trump Effort to Impound California Ballots
item.author: Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: In a 2-to-1 vote, an appeals court panel declined to order the state to set aside more than 20,000 mail-in ballots, calling the notion plainly unconstitutional.

item.title: Prosecutors Suggest They May Seek Additional Comey Charges
item.author: Devlin Barrett
item.content:encoded: At a hearing in federal court, prosecutors defended an unusual, 11th-hour criminal case accusing the former F.B.I. director of leaking classified information a decade ago.

item.title: Judge Appoints Special Master to Determine if Trump Officials Lied in Golf Course Suit
item.author: Zach Montague
item.content:encoded: Judge Ana C. Reyes said an outside investigator would help determine whether parks officials or Justice Department lawyers withheld plans for Washington’s East Potomac Park.

item.title: A Resurgent Justice Democrats Could Reshape a Democratic Congress
item.author: Catie Edmondson
item.content:encoded: Justice Democrats, which gained prominence backing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is on track to see more of its candidates elected. Will the party listen to them?
